subject: Clarifying Marketplace vs Direct Billing for Hosted API Commit Discounts
messages:
From: Alex Torres <procurement@acme-ai.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <cto@acme-ai.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Pricing structure questions (marketplace vs direct)

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — we like what Redwood brings on latency and the batching features. Before we proceed with a procurement path, we need clarity on how discounts interact with marketplace billing. Two quick questions: 

1) If we buy via AWS Marketplace (we're heavily using AWS), can Redwood apply the same per-token commit discount tiers as with direct billing? Any upstream marketplace fees that would reduce the effective discount?

2) If we sign a 12-month commit (expected 2.5B tokens/mo), is there a difference in how the invoice/contract looks between direct and marketplace? Our procurement prefers marketplace billing for consolidated invoices but finance is sensitive to net unit economics.

Can you share any documentation or a short note so our procurement/legal team can evaluate?

Thanks,
Alex
Procurement Manager, ACME AI

---
Attachment: ACME_RFP_scope.pdf (application/pdf)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Alex Torres <procurement@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <cto@acme-ai.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: Pricing structure questions (marketplace vs direct)

Alex —

Appreciate the clear questions. High-level answers up front, then I'll drop a short note on mechanics and attach our marketplace fee summary.

TL;DR:
- Direct billing: Redwood can apply standard per-token commit discounts and any negotiated uplift/rebate directly to your invoices.
- Marketplace billing (AWS/GCP/Azure): Marketplace platforms levy a seller fee (typically 10–20% depending on the program and region). That fee changes how we present discounts: often the list price shown on the marketplace is higher to account for the marketplace fee, and we provide an equivalent credit or adjusted pricing in our contract/commit paperwork where possible.
- Net effect: Your effective per-token price can be similar in both paths, but the purchase path affects invoice flow, accounting classification (AMEX/payable vs marketplace charge), and sometimes timing of credits.

I'm attaching a breakdown: Marketplace_fee_schedule.xlsx and our commit tier CSV so you can see example math for 2.5B tokens/mo. Key notes:
- Some enterprise programs on AWS allow private offers where the seller (Redwood) absorbs part of the marketplace fee enabling similar net-to-customer pricing as direct.
- Where the marketplace requires the full fee to be applied to list price, we typically offset with a credit line item in the first invoice cycle or via a monthly rebate. This is handled differently across GCP/Azure marketplaces.

I'll loop in Marissa for any commercial specifics; if ACME wants marketplace consolidation of invoices we can recommend the private offer path on AWS to keep net economics intact.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0112

Attachments: Marketplace_fee_schedule.xlsx, redwood-pricing-commit-tiers.csv
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFP: Pricing structure questions (marketplace vs direct)

Rishi / Naomi — quick internal note before we respond to Alex/Priya. Short bullets to align: 

- For 2.5B tokens/mo (12-month), direct commit margins are straightforward: we tier the per-token price, apply committed discount, and invoice monthly.
- AWS Marketplace: typical AWS take is 15% for public listings; private offers can reduce that to effectively 0% pass-through if we agree on discounting/contracting approach. But private offers take longer (legal + AWS onboarding).
- GCP Marketplace has different revenue-share rules and often requires billing via Google billing accounts — vertical coordination with finance is needed.
- Need to confirm ACME's procurement flexibility: do they require purchase via their AWS portal/chargeback, or would they accept a private offer where ACME still pays via AWS but the net unit economics are equalized?

Commercial options to propose (ranked by speed to close):
1) Direct contract with Redwood + monthly invoices (fastest, simplest for discounts).
2) AWS private offer — keeps consolidated billing in AWS and preserves net pricing; requires AWS POA + time for offer setup.
3) Public marketplace listing purchase — fastest from a buying UX but margin compression unless we take credit/rebate approach (and finance may treat credits differently).

Ask: Rishi, confirm typical timeline for private offer setup (we usually see 2–4 weeks if AWS has required docs on file). Also, what appetite do we have to absorb a portion of the marketplace fee to accelerate a close?

-Marissa
Director, Commercial Programs — Redwood Inference

---
Note: attaching internal template: Marketplace_fee_schedule.xlsx for modeling.
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP: Pricing structure questions (marketplace vs direct)

Internal quick reply with numbers so we can give ACME concrete options: 

Assumptions: 2.5B tokens/mo, baseline hosted price $0.0008 per token (list), commit discounts as follows: 10% @ 1B, 18% @ 2B, 25% @ 5B. For ACME target (2.5B) they land in the 18% band.

Option math (net per-token):
- Direct: $0.0008 * (1 - 0.18) = $0.000656 per token
- Public AWS Marketplace (15% fee applied to seller): list price must be increased to cover 15% fee. If we keep list at $0.0008, we receive $0.00068 after fee; after 18% commit discount applied on our side, customer effective price ends up slightly higher unless we issue a credit. Practically, to match direct net, we would set marketplace list ~ $0.00094 so that after 15% fee we net $0.000799 and can give same discount. That confuses buyer invoices.
- AWS Private Offer: can replicate direct net; we can structure a private pricing contract that preserves the same net price and still bills via AWS with consolidated invoice. Leads to minimal disruption for ACME finance.

Risk/operational notes:
- If procurement insists on public marketplace purchase for speed, offer a short-term rebate (monthly credit) to equalize first 3 months and then transition to private offer once set up.
- Legal: marketplace purchase T&Cs sometimes limit warranty/SLAs. Need Legal to confirm but we can usually add an SOW ride-along for SLAs.

My recommendation to include in reply: present 2 paths (Direct vs AWS Private Offer) with clear next steps and timelines. Offer to produce a table with invoice examples for ACME finance.

Rishi
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Alex Torres <procurement@acme-ai.com>, Priya Shah <cto@acme-ai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Options for ACME: Marketplace vs Direct (short summary + next steps)

Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the questions — below is a concise summary for procurement/finance and recommended next steps. If useful we can run the numbers in a short walkthrough with finance to show invoice examples.

Summary: 
- Direct purchase from Redwood: simplest from a commercial perspective. We can apply committed per-token discounts directly on your monthly invoices. Invoice appears from Redwood and posts as a standard vendor charge.

- AWS Marketplace (public): convenient for buyers but marketplaces apply a seller fee (commonly 10–20%). To keep our economics steady we either (A) raise list price and provide an off-invoice credit so your net per-token equals the direct price, or (B) run a limited-term rebate. This can make the payment/invoice lines look different and may complicate internal chargeback.

- AWS Private Offer (recommended if ACME wants consolidated AWS billing): allows the purchase to go through AWS while preserving net pricing identical to direct. Setup typically takes 2–4 weeks (legal + AWS onboarding).

Proposed next steps: 
1) Which billing path does ACME prefer in principle? (Direct invoice / Public marketplace / AWS private offer)
2) If AWS private offer: please confirm the AWS account ID and billing contact so we can initiate the private offer paperwork with AWS.
3) If timeline is tight and ACME needs to close this week: we can offer a short-term monthly credit on a public marketplace purchase to equalize net pricing and then transition to private offer within 30–45 days.

Attachments: Marketplace_fee_schedule.xlsx (line-item math), redwood-pricing-commit-tiers.csv, ACME_SOW_draft.pdf (SOW placeholder).

Happy to jump on a 30-min call with your procurement and finance to walk the invoice examples.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
